description: Reusable .NET 10 package that wraps ASP.NET Core Identity with cookie and JWT auth, Google OAuth, a pluggable e-mail provider, a multi-tenant model with dynamic RBAC (roles + module permissions), and secure defaults — wired up with a single AddMyIdentity call. JWT and Google OAuth secrets are supplied by the consumer (never shipped in the package).
releaseNotes: v5.12.0: the user listings ask for a permission, the key ring can live outside the site, a module can group others under a parent, and the residuals of the 5.12 audit are closed. IMyIdentityUserService.GetAllAsync and GetAllByTenantAsync are closed by default: they admit SystemAdmin, the tenant's TenantAdmin and a caller the permission decision point grants Read, or else Modify, on the identity module, tenant-wide; everyone else gets PermissionDenied, never an empty list (MyIdentityPermissionOptions.AllowTenantMembersToListUsers brings back 5.11; a new describer message to translate, AccessDeniedListUsers()). MyIdentityDataProtectionOptions.KeyRingLocation = UserProfile puts the key ring in the framework's folder for the account (two deployments with the same AppName under one account share it). Startup proves the user's DPAPI, fails on an undefined %VAR% in DataProtectionKeyPath, and treats a blank path as unset (move the existing key files). A refused API key is logged at Information for Malformed and UnknownId, and its challenge is appended to WWW-Authenticate. A tenant module can declare a Parent in code (MyIdentityModuleDefinition.Parent; MyIdentityPermissionOptions.GetParentModule and GetChildModules): a grant of the parent counts for each child, cut to what the child supports, with no schema change. A tenant policy name is read strictly, as the platform one is: a module code with ':' and a number after it no longer moves a page's policy to another module, and a malformed name fails with InvalidOperationException. Behaviour changes with the same signature, for a caller who is not a SystemAdmin: an id outside the caller's tenant and an id that does not exist get the same answer (UserNotFound, AssignmentNotFound, false or null; for a role, PermissionDenied, where a missing role got RoleNotFound), and a caller without Modify gets PermissionDenied for every account id. A session, the per-user permission question, the tenant gate's exemption and EnterTenantAsync take SystemAdmin and TenantAdmin only from the global role of that exact name, and CreateFirstSystemAdminAsync refuses a role row that would not make one (InvalidOperationException) and is serialized across instances on SQL Server. A call that signs a session in or out refuses a response that has already started, and the passkey members refuse a Blazor circuit. ResetPasswordWithTokenAsync and ConfirmEmailAsync answer LinkInvalidOrExpired for an account that does not exist or is bound to an API key, and the reset for one deleted or disabled too (it no longer returns false). LoginAsync answers LockedOut at the lockout threshold for every account. A mail sent inside a unit of work goes out after the commit. Every question of Modify on the identity module outside the gate of the user listings asks the decision point in one re-entry frame: a decision point that makes such a call while it answers one gets InvalidOperationException, with a new message. The library's writes lock each account they write before their first write, in the order of the ids, with an UPDATE that changes no value (it runs UPDATE triggers and raises a rowversion of the user type; enlist your contexts in your unit); SetTenantAdminAsync and RemoveTenantAdminAsync run their hook before their locks, as in 5.11, and answer ConcurrencyFailure when the account was written after they read it, by their hook too; an API key and a first interactive credential can no longer both be given on one instance, and no library write puts an account in a tenant while it is being deactivated (an entry waits and gets TenantInactive). IMyIdentityTenantService.UpdateAsync refuses a duplicate tenant name (so a TenantAdmin learns whether another tenant has a name), and a TradingName also collides under the login's rule, trimmed and case-insensitive. The authorization views hand the decision point a cancellable token and implement IDisposable. New startup warnings; a subclass of a gated service that re-implements its interface over a new member starts, with a warning; the audit's start check decides with the sink in use; behind a wrapper of the hosted services that forwards only StartAsync, the API key source and the key ring's check now run, and their errors stop the start. SQL Server is the only supported provider, in the documentation and in the code. No schema change; nothing removed or changed in the public surface, nothing added to an existing interface. The package validation baseline is 5.11.0. Upgrading from 5.11.0, with a table of what can break you: MyIdentity/UPGRADE.md §56.
